findings.reason: a bound that survives in s88 after the plan declares it moved is a duplicated mandatory measurement, and the bound measures the plan's own ordering.
findings.text: s90's Why states the live bound "moves here from s88", yet s88's done-when at plan.html:836 still reads verbatim "The live bound of s13 (under 20 MB/min and under 5% of one core over 60 s with at least 30 live runs) is measured once on the fleet node after the station reloads onto this node … and both figures are written in the RCA either way", the same sentence s90's done-when repeats — so s88's gate demands a figure only s90's three-reader change can reach, while s90 waits on s88 to land, and the same fleet measurement is a done-when in two sections (and a third time, as "under 20 MB/min", in s12's cutover at plan.html:371)

findings.reason: the node's single verdict is the parse bound, so three corrections that nothing measures ride to a close they were never checked on, and a reviewer closing the section signs for work the gate did not see.
findings.text: s90's Deliverable joins the endpoint (no steady reader reads a whole stream) with three unrelated corrections — `_StreamCursor.as_resume` "which has no caller, is wired or deleted", an RCA paragraph's attribution fixed, and `tests/test_watch_stream_parse_is_cached.py` near line 240 changed so a resumed answer that drops the earliest records fails — and the done-when asserts none of the three: it counts parsed bytes and compares answers, so a landing that leaves `as_resume` dead, leaves the RCA misattributed and leaves the exact-equality assertion in place still passes.

findings.reason: a worker held to the plan's stated mechanism and its named counter implements the plan's guess instead of the endpoint, and the review round is then spent testing that guess rather than the behaviour.
findings.text: the Deliverable prescribes implementation, not an endpoint: it fixes where state lives ("keeps the folded flags with the cursor rather than the decoded events;") and the fate of one internal symbol (`_StreamCursor.as_resume`), and the done-when fixes the accounting seam by requiring the count "through a recording stand-in on `_count_parsed_bytes`", so a worker who answers the readers' folds through a different counter or a different resume owner must reshape the read to match the plan's guess.
